summary: Mercury Analytics: stale KV cache after quantized kernel rollout -> hallucinated metadata appended and billing spike
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary rollout of a quantized kernel (PR #7823) on 2026-03-10 11:02 UTC we observed a class of production responses for Mercury Analytics where generated completions sporadically included an extra metadata suffix (e.g., '...analysis
_source:cached-kv-123') and, in several cases, duplicated the tail of a prior completion. This coincided with elevated retry traffic from their app and a subsequent billing spike.

Impact:
- Customer Mercury Analytics experienced partial response corruption for ~18 minutes (affecting ~2.3% of requests) and observed higher invoiceable token counts due to client-side retries after streaming disconnects.
- Customer temporarily throttled incoming requests and escalated to SRE.

Environment:
- prod-us-west-2, dedicated enterprise tenancy for Mercury Analytics, serving-runtime with mixed kernel variants (standard + quantized canary) behind smart routing.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send streaming chat requests with long prefix (3–6k tokens) to pinned model gpt-4o-xlarge-16k.
2) When request routed to canary quantized kernel on node that had an older KV cache layout, the stream would cut short, client retried, and final completion contained an appended token block that matched a previous completion fragment plus a small metadata tag.

Observed behavior / telemetry:
- Increased 499/408-like streaming disconnects on nodes running new kernel selector during 11:02–11:20 UTC.
- Spikes in duplicate-suffix frequency measured via response-diff telemetry.
- Billing metrics show a ~28% uplift in invoiceable tokens for the customer during the window.
- KV cache hit/miss logs indicated schema mismatch errors on a subset of GPU nodes (schema version v3 vs expected v4).

Relevant logs & dashboards:
- Kibana: /app/kibana#/discover?q=trace%3A%22SUP-246999%22
- Metrics: streaming_disconnects and duplicate_suffix_rate (dashboard 'Mercury - PostIncident 246999')
- Runtime node logs: kernel-selector WARN: kv_schema_mismatch on nodes gpu-pool-45a
comments: Support (2026-03-10 11:25 UTC) - Aisha: Customer reported 'we're seeing repeated fragments and extra metadata appended to outputs; our clients retried and our bill spiked'. Ticket opened and escalated to SRE.
SRE (2026-03-10 11:42 UTC) - Marco: Detected kv_schema_mismatch on a subset of canary nodes. Rolling back canary to stop new traffic; enabling forced routing to standard kernels for Mercury tenancy.
Customer (2026-03-10 12:05 UTC) - Lydia Chen (Mercury): Confirmed behavior stops after routing change; provided sample payloads containing the appended suffix for analysis.
SRE (2026-03-10 12:40 UTC) - Marco: Performed targeted cache invalidation and node restart for affected GPU hosts. Observed duplicate-suffix rate fall to baseline by 12:52 UTC.
Support (2026-03-12 09:10 UTC) - Aisha: Customer provided log extracts; billing team preparing adjustment proposal. Creating follow-up action items and post-incident notes.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: quantized kernel introduced a KV cache on-disk layout change that the kernel-selector did not gate by schema version, causing older cache entries to be interpreted incorrectly.
Corroborating evidence: node logs show 'kv_schema_mismatch' warnings and the response diff tool shows repeated token spans that match cached entries from previous requests to the same node.

Routing analysis: Smart-router incorrectly flagged canary nodes as compatible for Mercury traffic because model fingerprint matched, but cache schema compatibility was not part of the compatibility check.
Reproduction: Simulated long-prefix streaming against affected node image reproduced truncated stream + appended cached suffix in dev by restoring an old cache blob and invoking the quantized kernel.
resolution_notes: Immediate mitigation: rolled back canary quantized kernel across the affected GPU pool at 11:50 UTC and routed Mercury tenancy traffic to known-good standard kernels.

Remediation steps applied: forced KV cache invalidation on affected hosts, restarted runtime processes, and deployed a hotfix to kernel-selector to include cache schema version in compatibility checks (hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7831).
Customer billing: Billing team provisionally credited Mercury Analytics for the affected window pending finalized invoice adjustment (internal billing reference BL-3342).
follow_up_actions: Add cache schema version check to rollout gating and smart-router compatibility matrix (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-03-18).
Create a canary smoke test that replays long-prefix streaming patterns and validates no appended cached fragments before advancing rollout (owner: qa/ci, due: 2026-03-16).
Instrument new alert for 'duplicate_suffix_rate' above 0.5% per tenancy to trigger automated rollback (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-15).
Finalize billing reconciliation with Mercury and complete formal credit; support to provide itemized token delta and runbook of mitigations (owner: billing/support, due: 2026-03-14).
Postmortem write-up and cross-team review scheduled (postmortem page link to follow).
